summary: Points 4 (Unified Mode: casual_direct_reply reuses admin advisor house rules) and 6 (RAG contamination root-cause: _MIN_SCORE 0.25→0.42 + low_confidence exclusion + logger wiring) tested end-to-end. Added new test file /app/backend/tests/test_intent_gateway_points_4_6_2026_01.py with 20 tests covering (a) source-level assertion that casual_direct_reply calls get_active_house_rules('advisor',None) + format_house_rules_block, (b) monkeypatched async tests proving graceful no-op when rules are OFF (default Preview state), correct prepending when ON, and swallowed exception when the lookup itself raises, (c) _MIN_SCORE == 0.42, (d) _quality_filter excludes low_confidence=True, accepts False/missing, preserves mode-C pass_result gate, (e) _rebuild_index projection now includes low_confidence, (f) log_conversational signature has low_confidence=False default and _build_log stores it, (g) chat_stream's log_conversational call site passes low_confidence=_low_confidence, (h) chat_send body contains ZERO log_conversational matches (pre-existing scope boundary confirmed), (i) Point 3 acceptance-bar regression re-verified live on both /chat/send and /chat/stream on a contaminated session + tool-request follow-up still routes to orchestrator, (j) admin insights /confidence-checks and /cost-alert endpoints unaffected. Also re-ran the full prior Point 3 suite (test_intent_gateway_casual_boundary_2026_01.py) — 21/21 still pass. Combined: 41/41 = 100%.

point_by_point_results.live_double_mismatch_trigger: SKIPPED — impractical to force reliably in Preview without extensive setup; per review request this is acceptable when wiring is confirmed by code review, which it is (chat_stream passes low_confidence=_low_confidence at the log_conversational call site, and _build_log persists it).

critical_code_review_comments: Point 4 implementation is clean: house_rules lookup is wrapped in try/except with a pass-through no-op — the code path can never regress into a hard dependency on the DB, matching the founder's 'never a hard dependency' rule. The order (house rules FIRST, then base casual system prompt) also matches the admin-rules-are-highest-priority contract in services/house_rules.py format_house_rules_block.

Point 6 has both prongs wired correctly: retriever raises the bar (0.42) at read time AND excludes low_confidence rows from ever being indexed, so a future retriever rebuild permanently forgets past fallback turns. _rebuild_index projection now includes low_confidence (verified in source), so the exclusion actually takes effect at index-build time, not just at score time.

Pre-existing scope boundary flagged in the review request is real and confirmed: chat_send's body contains ZERO log_conversational() calls (regex-verified over the function's byte range in routers/chat.py). If a future change adds one, the test test_chat_send_does_not_call_log_conversational will fail loudly — good tripwire for keeping the wiring consistent.
seed_data_creation: None — tests use unique session_ids per run (uuid4 hex) and don't mutate house_rules doc.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Point 3 + Point 4 + Point 6 are all green as of this run. Two pytest suites cover this surface: test_intent_gateway_casual_boundary_2026_01.py (21 tests) and test_intent_gateway_points_4_6_2026_01.py (20 tests). Both hit live /api/aurem-dev/chat/{send,stream} with the exact founder acceptance-bar message on a contaminated session and also do source-level checks on the retriever/logger wiring so future refactors that break the low_confidence pipeline will fail loudly. If house_rules toggles ever get flipped on in Preview, expect casual replies to visibly change (that's by design — Unified Mode). The Point 4 monkeypatched test asserts the ORDER: house_rules block first, then casual system prompt second — do not swap this without updating the test.
